# Incident: jp-mirror-translator Subagent Places JP Warning Before Frontmatter

## Date

2026-05-30

## What happened

When `work-kit:jp-mirror-translator` was used to create `SKILL.jp.md` (for the new `config` skill),
the subagent placed the JP mirror warning comment **before** the YAML frontmatter:

```md
<!-- This file is a Japanese mirror. ... -->  ← placed BEFORE frontmatter (WRONG)

---
name: config
description: |
  ...
---
<!-- Generated by work-kit/work-start v2.38.0 -->
(content)
```

The correct structure is:

```md
---
name: config
description: |
  ...
---
<!-- Generated by work-kit/work-start v2.38.0 -->
<!-- This file is a Japanese mirror. ... -->  ← after frontmatter (CORRECT)
(content)
```

## Why it happened

- The `jp-mirror-translator` agent (claude-haiku) generated the file with the warning at the very top.
- The agent follows a general "add warning at top" heuristic and does not correctly detect YAML frontmatter.
- This breaks GitHub Markdown rendering: the `---` after a comment is rendered as a horizontal rule instead of frontmatter.

## Fix applied

After `jp-mirror-translator` completed, manually edited `SKILL.jp.md` to move the warning comment
from line 1 to immediately after the closing `---` of the frontmatter.

## Prevention

After every `jp-mirror-translator` invocation that creates or updates a file with YAML frontmatter,
always verify the comment block position:
1. If the file starts with `---`, the JP mirror warning must appear **after** the closing `---`.
2. If the file has no frontmatter, the top-of-file position is correct.
3. Never place any HTML comment before the opening `---` of YAML frontmatter.

Note: This is a different root cause from the incident `agent-jp-mirror-stamp-before-frontmatter.md`
(which covers manual JP mirror creation without `mark-generated`). Here the issue is the
`jp-mirror-translator` subagent's automatic behavior.
